summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -2 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl 0; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Coffee +14.4%; weakest: KC wheat -14.8%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.96% (+0 bp in a month), 2-year 4.65% (-6 bp); 2s10s curve +31 bp (+6 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.02% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.62 (+1.0% in a month, +3.4% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.052 (-1.1% in a month): little changed. USD/CNY 6.665 (-0.5%); USD/MXN 18.72 (+8.3%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -1.3% in a month (+11.9% YTD); VIX 19.0. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 98.95 $/bbl (+12.5% in a month), Brent 112.80, ULSD 4.751 $/gal (+4.4%), natural gas 2.78 (-10.8%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -6.3% in a month, Shanghai Composite -7.4%, Hang Seng -8.6%, yuan +0.5% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 14 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (42%); S&P GSCI +2.1% in a month; gold -7.6%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
